_comment: Short 5 in docs/CONTENT.md: balance billing, and the sentence to read down the phone. The payload is the sentence, not the explanation.
_injury: Fell off a ladder, arm in a sling: already treated, now arguing about the bill.
_pacing: The hook was three ideas in one line (fell, insurance paid, clinic billed) and the drawing had no room. Now the fall is its own line, the clinic is a second, and the two envelopes arrive on a third, so each image gets a beat.
_envelopes: The two documents arrive as envelopes with pages sliding out, the same way Short 1 shows them. It is the series' image for paperwork turning up, and it puts the two numbers side by side before the argument starts.
_stakes: The highest-stakes Short in the set: it tells someone not to pay a bill. The limit is spoken as the word is named (in network) and written on the board (out of network, the rules differ), and the disclaimer is drawn rather than left to a description.
_naming: House style says name the word within ten seconds. Here it lands at about twenty-five, and the reason is that the surprise is the second envelope: the word is named in the line immediately after it, which is the rule's intent.
_numbers: Three, all round: charged $1,000, allowed $400, and the $600 between them. The sentence says 'what I owe' rather than a fourth figure.
_pronunciation: 'EOB' is written as one word: Studio-Q reads it as letters, verified by synthesising it and running Whisper back over it. Spelling it 'E O B' made the caption break the letters across lines.

variants.sling: You fell off a ladder and broke your arm.

body.text: The clinic set it, put your arm in a sling, and sent you home.
A few weeks later, two envelopes turn up.
Your insurance letter says the visit was allowed at four hundred dollars, and it paid its share.
Then the clinic billed you a thousand.
That has a name. It is balance billing, and if the clinic is in your network, it is not allowed.
The six hundred dollars between those two numbers is the discount the clinic agreed to when it joined the network.
So it comes off the bill. It does not come to you.
Call the number on the bill, and read this out.
You are in my network. My EOB says what I owe. Please correct the balance. Out of network, the rules are different.
Check yours before you dispute. Or upload them free at UseClaimRight.com.
